text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected: elevated 5xx on gateway (502/504) in us-west-2. error-rate 12% -> paging oncall. brief: increased upstream timeouts + sporadic proxy errors.

tara: saw the alert, looking at ingress LB metrics now. recreating spike in GA dashboard.

mike_oncall: i'm oncall for the day, grabbing context. any customer-facing errors reported yet?

kelsey_support: few support tickets coming in—customers seeing intermittent uploads failing. severity: P1-ish for a handful of high-traffic tenants.

ashley: stack traces are sparse. most requests don't have request_id in logs. looks like header propagation failed on a roll earlier today.

tara: yep, traces are missing spanids too. sampling ok but no parent ids. observability gap is making root cause hard.

mike_oncall: can we enable temporary verbose proxy logging + inject request ids at the edge? need short-term telemetry to correlate.

ashley: I can flip a stopgap config on the proxy pool. plan: enable X-Request-Id generation + debug headers, 10m retention to S3. Doing a non-prod test first.

ashley: TEST COMMAND (non-prod):
```
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/proxy-bastion -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/debug/config -d '{"inject_request_id":true,"debug_headers":true}'
```

tara: once that's validated, we'll push to prod on a single canary node. I'll monitor error rate and latency.

mike_oncall: please also add a short-lived metric to track presence of request_id header: proxy.request_id.missing.count -> helps quantify scope.

ashley: added a metric in the patch: proxy.request_id.missing.count (delta). Can be queried in GA.

incident-bot: CHANGE: config patch scheduled for prod canary at +8m by ashley.

sam_prod: heads-up—alerted SalesOps for affected customers, prepping comms if we see >10% tenant impact.

kelsey_support: flagged two customers for immediate outreach. sending brief status notes.

tara: canary pushed. initial observations: 1 node shows request_ids now, request_id missing count dropped on that node to ~2%. overall system error-rate down 4% in canary traffic slice.

mike_oncall: good sign. what's the fallback plan if error rate doesn't drop after full rollout?

ashley: fallback: revert config and scale proxy pool to handle backlog (add 3 nodes) + enable retry path to gateway-v2 which has higher timeout conservative settings. running a dry-run of the retry config.

tara: also enabling temporary 60s increased upstream timeout in the gateway routing policy to reduce 504s while we stabilize. will monitor latencies.

incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: error-rate (global) reduced from 12% -> 7% after canary, p95 latency +40ms.

mike_oncall: seems like missing request_id propagation contributed to blind spots that slowed mitigation. need a postmortem action: ensure request_id auto-injection at edge is enforced by policy, not optional.

sam_prod: agreed. also need runbook addition: if traces missing, enable proxy injection and canary within 10 minutes.

kelsey_support: will update the customer-impact log with affected tenants and outreach timestamps.

ashley: rolling out full patch now (staggered 5 nodes every 2m). watching logs tail:
```
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=proxy --tail=100 | grep X-Request-Id | wc -l
```

tara: after first 3 nodes, global error-rate at 3.8%. will continue rollout.

mike_oncall: keeping pager escalation threshold adjusted. if errors creep >6% revert to fallback.

incident-bot: NOTE: temporary verbose logs will be auto-pruned in 30m; upload retention to S3 will be limited to 1 hour.

ashley: full rollout completed. final check: request_id missing count ~0.9%, error-rate stabilized ~2.5%. latency within SLO.

tara: closing active mitigation. recommended follow-ups:
- permanent policy to enforce request_id injection at LB
- add unit/integration test for header propagation during deploys
- improve trace sampling fallback so traces survive when parent-id missing

mike_oncall: grabbing oncall handoff notes for next shift. will file follow-up ticket and link to this thread. tagging @next-oncall in handoff.

sam_prod: thanks everyone. I'll coordinate comms for customers who asked for post-incident details.

kelsey_support: sent update to affected customers, marking as "monitoring resolved".

incident-bot: INCIDENT resolved: root cause likely partial proxy config rollout that disabled request_id propagation. impact: transient increase in 5xx/timeouts. mitigation: temporary request_id injection, canary rollout, timeout tuning. Postmortem required.

mike_oncall: handing off to night shift. all notes in the ticket. good job team. :thumbsup:
